decisions.boundary_condition: Do not infer preferences for other room amenities, hotel types, destinations, dates, or prices.
decisions.canonical_value: Prefer hotel rooms with both an in-room coffee maker and a mini-fridge.
decisions.condition: When searching for or comparing hotel rooms.
decisions.default_action: Use both an in-room coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge as soft amenity criteria.
decisions.exception_condition: If otherwise suitable options lack either amenity, confirm whether the preference should be relaxed rather than automatically rejecting them.
decisions.name: Prefer an in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge
decisions.preference_value: Prefer hotel rooms with both a coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge.
decisions.rationale: The paired coffee-maker and mini-fridge preference is independently repeated across three hotel searches and is appropriately framed as a soft amenity preference.

decisions.boundary_condition: Treat this as a soft default unless the user explicitly makes breakfast mandatory; do not infer a specific breakfast quality standard.
decisions.canonical_value: Prefer hotels that include free breakfast.
decisions.condition: When searching for or comparing hotels for an overnight trip, consider free breakfast after satisfying explicit core constraints such as location, room or bed needs, budget, and required hotel class.
decisions.default_action: Rank or surface hotels with free breakfast higher, and confirm whether a candidate includes it when the amenity is unclear.
decisions.exception_condition: Relax or ignore this preference if the user says breakfast is unimportant, no suitable hotel satisfying higher-priority constraints includes it, or the user knowingly chooses a hotel without it.
decisions.name: Prefer hotels with included breakfast
decisions.preference_value: Prefer a hotel that includes free breakfast.
decisions.rationale: Free breakfast recurs across multiple hotel searches, but the evidence varies in strength and supports retaining it as a soft ranking preference rather than a universal hard filter or a specific quality requirement.
